evidence.quote:
There were no prisons, no slums, no insane asylums, no cripples, no
poverty, no wars.
evidence.paraphrase: The society is described as having eliminated social ills such as prisons, poverty, and wars.

evidence.quote: All diseases were conquered. So was old age.
evidence.paraphrase: Disease and aging have been eliminated in this world.

evidence.quote:
The population of the United States was stabilized at forty-million
souls.
evidence.paraphrase: The national population is held fixed at forty million people.

evidence.quote:
Wehling was fifty-six, a mere stripling in a population whose average
age was one hundred and twenty-nine.
evidence.paraphrase: A fifty-six-year-old is considered young because the average age is 129, contrasting with the reader's expectations.

evidence.quote:
The room was being redecorated. It was being redecorated as a memorial
to a man who had volunteered to die.
evidence.paraphrase: A room is being dedicated as a memorial to someone who chose to be terminated.

evidence.quote:
A sardonic old man, about two hundred years old, sat on a stepladder,
painting a mural he did not like.
evidence.paraphrase: A character is about two hundred years old, indicating extended lifespans.

evidence.quote:
"To be or not to be" was the telephone number of the municipal gas
chambers of the Federal Bureau of Termination.
evidence.paraphrase: A government bureau operates gas chambers reachable by a telephone number for voluntary death.

evidence.quote:
A curious thing about gas-chamber hostesses was that, no matter how lovely
and feminine they were when recruited, they all sprouted mustaches
within five years or so.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrative notes an odd physical change among gas-chamber hostesses over time.

evidence.quote:
The law said that no newborn child could survive unless the parents of
the child could find someone who would volunteer to die.
evidence.paraphrase: A legal rule requires a volunteer death before a newborn is allowed to live.

evidence.quote:
"All I have to do is pick
out which one of the triplets is going to live, then deliver my maternal
grandfather to the Happy Hooligan, and come back here with a receipt."
evidence.paraphrase: Wehling bitterly describes having to choose one triplet to live and take his grandfather to be terminated.

evidence.quote:
Would you like to go back to the good old days, when the population of
the Earth was twenty billion--about to become forty billion, then eighty
billion, then one hundred and sixty billion?
evidence.paraphrase: Dr. Hitz explains the rationale for population control by citing exponential population growth.

evidence.quote:
Without population
control, human beings would now be packed on this surface of this old
planet like drupelets on a blackberry!
evidence.paraphrase: Hitz argues that without population control humanity would be overcrowded.

evidence.quote:
In the year 2000," said Dr. Hitz, "before scientists stepped in and
laid down the law, there wasn't even enough drinking water to go around,
and nothing to eat but sea-weed
evidence.paraphrase: Hitz describes a past crisis of scarce water and food that scientists intervened to resolve.

evidence.quote:
Wehling shot Dr. Hitz dead. "There's room for one--a great big one," he
said.
evidence.paraphrase: Wehling murders Dr. Hitz to make room for one of his children.

evidence.quote: And then he shot himself, making room for all three of his children.
evidence.paraphrase: Wehling kills himself so all three of his children may live.

evidence.quote:
He knew that he would never paint again. He let his paintbrush fall to
the dropcloths below.
evidence.paraphrase: The painter, shaken, resolves to stop painting.

evidence.quote:
"All right," said the painter, "fit me in, if you please." And he gave
her his name, spelling it out.
evidence.paraphrase: The painter calls the termination bureau to schedule his own death.

evidence.quote:
"Thank you, sir," said the hostess. "Your city thanks you; your country
thanks you; your planet thanks you. But the deepest thanks of all is
from future generations."
evidence.paraphrase: The termination hostess thanks the caller on behalf of society for choosing to die.
